newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Southern starts 1.1-bln-yuan glass project.
newsitem.headline: China Southern starts 1.1-bln-yuan glass project.

text.p: Shenzhen-based China Southern Glass Holdings Co Ltd started production of its 1.1-billion-yuan super-thin float glass project on Tuesday, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.

Construction began in early 1995 on the project, which is designed to turn out 135,000 tonnes of float glass worth 500 million yuan a year and will become the company's chief source of profits in the coming years, it said.

A company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin the project would generate net earnings of about 60 million yuan in 1997 and more than 100 million yuan in 1998 when it became fully operational.
About 80 percent of the float glass will be sold domestically, with the remaining 20 percent exported to Southeast Asia and the United States, the official said.
He said Southern Glass's net profits this year would roughly equal the 1995 level of 134.67 million yuan.
The company said in its interim report for 1996 that it posted net earnings of 70.16 million yuan in the first half of 1996, down from the year-earlier level of 81.67 million.
The firm did not state whether the interim results were compiled under Chinese or international accounting standards.

Southern Glass blamed the lower earnings on worsening competition in the Chinese market from domestic rivals and weaker demand, which forced the firm to cut prices on a range of glass products to maintain market share.
